headline: Leaning higher
text: US futures are up today (S&P +1.37%, Nasdaq +2.73%), with Europe higher and Asia mostly up.
Helping: Europe, Asia, Copper, S&P 500 vs 200-day, Stocks above 200-day. Weighing: Dollar index.
Options price a typical day of about ±1.1% for the S&P 500 (about 7,548–7,719); historically about 82% of days stay inside that.

On past days with VIX between 15 and 20 and the VIX curve normal (since 1990, 1,616 days), the next session closed higher 54% of the time (all days: 54%), with a typical move of 0.5% (all days: 0.5%).

drivers.name: US futures
drivers.note: S&P +1.37% · Nasdaq +2.73% vs the last close. Live index futures.

drivers.name: Dollar index
drivers.note: A sharply stronger dollar usually weighs on US stocks (tighter money, weaker overseas earnings).

drivers.name: 10-year yield
drivers.note: At 5.00%. Fast-rising yields hurt growth and tech stocks; falling yields help them.

drivers.name: WTI oil
drivers.note: $87.04. A big oil jump feeds inflation worries; energy stocks move with it.

drivers.name: Gold
drivers.note: $3998. A strong gold bid often means investors are looking for safety.

drivers.name: Copper
drivers.note: “Dr. Copper”: rising copper = traders expect more growth.

drivers.name: Bitcoin
drivers.note: Trades all weekend and night: a read on risk appetite while Wall Street is shut.

drivers.name: S&P 500 vs 200-day
drivers.note: Above the 200-day = long-term uptrend: dips have tended to get bought.

drivers.name: Stocks above 200-day
drivers.note: How many big US stocks are in their own uptrend.

drivers.name: VIX
drivers.note: Below 16 calm, above 25 nervous, above 30 fear.

drivers.name: VIX curve
drivers.note: Normal (below 1): no panic in the options market.

drivers.name: Market mood
drivers.note: Greed: the site's 0–100 fear/greed gauge from 10 readings. Extremes often mark turning points, so it sets the tone rather than the direction.

levels.name: SPY call wall
levels.note: Biggest call position: often acts as a ceiling. Was 750 before the open.

levels.name: SPY put wall
levels.note: Biggest put position: often acts as a floor; a break can speed up selling. Was 750 before the open.

levels.name: SPY gamma flip
levels.note: Above it dealers calm moves down; below it they speed them up. Was 755 before the open.

base.label: VIX between 15 and 20 and the VIX curve normal

scenarios.text: If SPY breaks below 760 (call wall), selling can speed up.
Yesterday's S&P 500 range was 7,572–7,645: a break of either end is the first real sign of direction.

tips: 9 of the 12 Focus setups point the same way as the lean (9 long, 3 short).
Crypto: fear & greed 29 (Fear), Bitcoin +1.1% in 24h, funding 0.005%.
